La alerta cubre la carga de DLL mediante rundll32 (T1218.011), la ejecución de scripts con cmd (T1059.003) y las llamadas a la API nativa (T1106). Revise CommandLine para identificar la DLL o el .bat referenciado y su ruta completa. Anote el punto de entrada que se pasa a rundll32.

Busque en el mismo host, en una ventana de +/- 15 minutos, conexiones de red, archivos creados en C:\Windows\Temp, servicios nuevos o cambios en el registro.
Identifique el usuario de la ejecución y verifique sus inicios de sesión recientes y su actividad en otros equipos.
Busque alertas previas del mismo host o usuario y la presencia de estos nombres de archivo en otros endpoints.

Si no está autorizado, aísle el endpoint de la red y preserve la memoria y los artefactos antes de hacer cambios.

en.summary: rundll32.exe or cmd.exe ran with a command line that references artifacts of the RedMimicry Winnti playbook (gthread-3.6.dll, sigcmm-2.4.dll or \Windows\Temp\tmp.bat). This may be an authorized breach emulation or unauthorized use of the tool.
en.what_it_detects: Process creation events where Image ends with \rundll32.exe or \cmd.exe and CommandLine contains gthread-3.6.dll, sigcmm-2.4.dll or \Windows\Temp\tmp.bat. These file names are used by the Winnti playbook of RedMimicry, an automated breach emulation tool.
en.why_it_matters: RedMimicry reproduces techniques publicly attributed to the Winnti group. The alert covers DLL loading through rundll32 (T1218.011), script execution with cmd (T1059.003) and native API calls (T1106). If nobody authorized an exercise, the host may be compromised.
triage_steps: Check with the red team or security team whether a RedMimicry emulation is authorized for this host and time window.
Review CommandLine to find the referenced DLL or .bat and its full path. Note the entry point passed to rundll32.
Inspect ParentImage and the process tree: what launched rundll32 or cmd, and which child processes followed.
Get the hash of gthread-3.6.dll, sigcmm-2.4.dll or tmp.bat. Check its reputation and when it was created on disk.
On the same host, within +/- 15 minutes, look for network connections, files created in C:\Windows\Temp, new services or registry changes.
Identify the user who ran the process. Check their recent logons and their activity on other machines.
Look for earlier alerts for the same host or user, and for these file names on other endpoints.
false_positives: Authorized adversary emulation or purple team exercises that use the RedMimicry Winnti playbook.
Detection validation tests in labs or on SOC test hosts.
response_steps: If the exercise is authorized, document it, check detection coverage and close the alert with the exercise ticket reference.
If it is not authorized, isolate the endpoint from the network and preserve memory and artifacts before you change anything.
Collect the DLLs and the .bat for analysis, and block their hashes in the EDR.
Verify any persistence before you remove it, reset the affected user's credentials and hunt for the same indicators across the fleet.
If compromise is confirmed, rebuild the host from a trusted image and monitor it closely afterward.
en.severity_rationale: High fits because the file names are specific to an offensive tool and have no known legitimate use outside authorized exercises.
